description: Opaque person key. Hash your institutional ID with a salt you keep. Same key in every file and every in-cycle export.
Intended entry year (fall-term year for fall entrants).
Intended entry term.
Actual entry year if different from the intended year (deferral, or entered in another term). Blank if the same. Deferrals are common in law; send for every admit who deferred.
Actual entry term if different from the intended term. Blank if the same.

What kind of entrant this is. Other types go to a separate file or are excluded. 1L = first-year JD entrant. Transfer = enters the second year or later from another JD program. Visiting and non-JD entrants are excluded.
Level of the program applied to.
Program or division the student applied to, as you record it. For example JD full-time, JD part-time or evening, joint-degree partner. Send your own labels and what they mean.
allowed_values_or_notes: Free text with a code list

description: Full-time or part-time at entry. Use the ABA full-time and part-time definitions.
Intended major or program of study at application. Concentration or certificate, only if recorded at application.
allowed_values_or_notes: Free text with a code list

description: Residency at application, based on the known physical address at the time of application. Resident or nonresident of the state where the school sits. Say if your 509 filing uses a different basis.
Residency class used for billing, only if it differs from `residency`.
State plus the first three ZIP digits (ZIP3), from the permanent address at application. Never the full ZIP. ZIP5 goes only in the optional `zip_key` file.
Metropolitan or micropolitan area code. If you send it, produce it with the script we supply, before addresses are removed.
Distance-to-campus band from the same script.

Raw label for the earliest recorded contact. Do not recode. Send if you record prospects (list purchases, fairs and forums, events, web inquiries). If you do not, leave blank and set first_touch_is_application to true for everyone.
allowed_values_or_notes: Free text; we map it with a versioned source taxonomy

description: Date of the earliest recorded contact (converted to days before term start, then dropped).
True when the application is the first recorded contact (stealth applicant).
Date the person became a prospect or inquiry.
Date the application was started.
Date the application was complete and actionable (all required items received). Use the date the file was complete for review, and say if that differs from the submission date.
Admission plan the applicant applied under. Binding early decision, if you offer it; otherwise regular or rolling.
allowed_values_or_notes: Early decision; Early action; Restrictive early action; Regular; Rolling

description: Final admission decision at the term census. Applicants placed on a waiting list and never admitted are their own category.
allowed_values_or_notes: Admitted; Denied; Waitlisted not admitted; Withdrawn before decision; Incomplete

description: Date of the admission decision (the offer date for admits).
Label of the batch or wave in which the decision or offer was released. Needed to define waves (methodology section 4). Waves are separate only if offers go out in batches at least three weeks apart.
Date the applicant was placed on the waiting list, if any.
Date a waitlisted applicant was offered admission, if any.
allowed_values_or_notes: Blank if not admitted from the list

description: Date the first enrollment (seat) deposit was received. If you take a second deposit, send its date in `second_deposit_date`.
Date the second deposit was received, if you use two deposits.
Enrolled at the official census date of the entry term. One definition for every cohort. Reconciles to your ABA 509 matriculants (see Institutional reference).
Date of withdrawal before census, if any.
Enrolled at the census of the next fall term. Second-year (2L) enrollment.
Enrolled at the census two falls later. Third-year (3L) enrollment.
Number of recorded campus visits before the admit decision. Visits and open-house attendance, if recorded.
allowed_values_or_notes: Counts before the decision date only

description: Number of recorded events attended before the decision date.
Count of meaningful two-way contacts (calls, meetings, replies) before the decision date.
Which admission test the applicant submitted. Send the raw scores and the test type. Do not convert or impute.
LSAT score used for your reporting and your index. State in the dictionary whether this is the highest or the average of multiple scores, and use the same rule in every year.
Whether `lsat_score` is the highest or the average score.
Undergraduate GPA used for your reporting and your index.
Who calculated the UGPA. LSAC-calculated (CAS) or school-calculated.
GRE verbal reasoning score, if the applicant submitted the GRE. Raw score only. We apply a published concordance where one exists; otherwise UGPA is used alone.
GRE quantitative reasoning score, if submitted.
JD-Next score, if submitted.
Full-time work experience in whole years, if recorded.
First-generation status. Blank if unknown. Do not code unknown as No.
IPEDS categories. Used only to audit results for fairness. Never a model input, grid dimension or target.
As recorded. Used only to audit results for fairness.
Age in whole years at the application date. Not the date of birth.
Veteran or active military status.
Alumni family connection.
True if the student receives aid under rules outside the normal process.
Why the student is excluded. Tuition remission or exchange, employee dependent, stipend or fellowship, named full-tuition scholar, joint-degree award, or other.
allowed_values_or_notes: Free text with a code list

description: Same key as students.
Aid year.
Applied for federal aid (FAFSA) for this aid year.
Date your office received the first FAFSA record.
EFC (aid years through 2023-24) or SAI (2024-25 and later). Required only if need is part of your scholarship decisions or loan-eligibility analysis.
EFC or SAI. The two are not comparable without this label.
Dependent or independent.
Selected for verification.
Date verification was completed.
allowed_values_or_notes: Blank if not selected or not completed

description: Methodology used to determine need for institutional aid.
Need as determined by your institutional methodology (CSS Profile or your own form), if you use one.
Household income band from the aid application, only where you package on income or no need index exists. Banded, never exact.
Cost-of-attendance budget used to package this student, if it varies by student.
Same key as students. One row per student, fund and package version.
Aid year.
Your fund code. Send a crosswalk (file `fund_crosswalk`).
Standard component we map the fund code to. You may leave it blank; we map from the crosswalk.
Annual amount offered, in dollars.
allowed_values_or_notes: Never blank. Zero only if you offered zero. Unknown is blank, never zero

description: Date this amount was first communicated to the student.
allowed_values_or_notes: Required to exclude aid not known at the decision date

description: Package revision number (1 = first offer). Tier 1: the final package only. Tier 2: every version.
Amount the student accepted. Post-decision; excluded from price models.
Amount disbursed. Post-enrollment; excluded from price models.
Whether the award renews.
How the award renews. Fixed dollars or a percentage of tuition.
allowed_values_or_notes: Fixed dollars; Percent of tuition; Other

description: Conditions to keep the award (GPA, class rank, credits), stated exactly. If your scholarships are conditional, the exact threshold and the year it is tested.
Numeric threshold for the condition (for example a minimum GPA). Only if a numeric condition exists.
Number of years the award is committed for. Usually three for a full-time JD award.
True for any part of an award that exceeds tuition (a stipend). Stipends are an excluded component in total-award mode.
Why a later version differs from the one before it.
allowed_values_or_notes: Student request; Documented competing offer; Staff-initiated; Appeal; Other

description: Date the student asked for reconsideration, if applicable.
For PLUS loans only: who applied. Grad PLUS (grandfathered borrowers).
For PLUS loans only: credit decision.
For PLUS loans only: date of the credit decision.
Your fund code, as it appears in aid_offers.
Name of the fund or scholarship.
Standard component (see the component table).
Gift or self-help.
Who funds it.
The fund's own eligibility rule.
True if staff can award from the fund at their discretion (the flexible pool).
True if awards from the fund follow rules outside the normal process.
First date the fund was used.
Last date the fund was used, if retired.
Entry year.
Program the price applies to.
Residency group the price applies to, if prices differ.
How tuition is billed. Annual flat rate, per credit hour, or per quarter. If per credit, send credit hours per year.
Published annual tuition, in dollars.
Credit hours billed in a standard full-time year. Required if billed per credit.
Mandatory fees that every full-time student pays.
On-campus food and housing.
Standard housing and food budget used in your cost of attendance.
Average books and supplies.
Transportation budget.
Personal and other cost-of-attendance items.
Planned tuition increase for the next entering class, if decided.
Entry year the policy applies to.
Program the policy applies to.

Whether the scholarship award is the whole institutional award or a supplement on top of formula awards. Total institutional scholarship (law default) or supplement after formula awards (undergraduate default).

The grid, matrix or index that sets awards: thresholds (test, GPA, index) and award amounts, with effective dates. If you have no published threshold, say so and describe how awards are decided. That is common in law and means we cannot estimate a price anchor from history.
Effective dates for each version of the grid and any change in thresholds or amounts.
Who decides awards and how: committee, matrix, discretionary, or a mix.
How institutional need grants are computed. Only if need drives any award.
Annual discretionary aid budget, and the rules for appeals. Total institutional scholarship budget for the entering class.
Amount set aside for appeals and reconsideration, if any.
Board or president target for the institutional discount rate.
Target entering-class headcount by student type.
Whether the class target is a hard seat cap or a soft target.
Accepted band around the class target, as a percent (for example 3, 5 or 10). Mandatory. The price-test verdict depends on it.
Class-profile targets you manage to (for example median LSAT and UGPA).
Minimum awards or limits on change for particular groups.
Largest cut any group's award may take, as a percent of tuition.
Whether any scholarship is conditional on performance.
Can staff deliver a test bonus as a formula line, with no test flag in the CRM or aid system? This decides whether the all-eligible analysis is primary (methodology section 4).
Who sees award details and test membership.
Entry year.
What the date is.

The date.
Deposit amount, for deposit events.
Whether and until when the deposit is refundable, for deposit events.

Award year (1 = first year).
Aid year.
Amount actually renewed for that year.
Outcome of renewal.

description: Reason for any reduction or loss.
allowed_values_or_notes: GPA; Class rank; Credits; Withdrew; Other

True if assigned to the test; false for eligible admits left out.
Date the random assignment was made.
Stratum used for blocked randomization. Position band by wave.
Bonus aid added for this student. Top arm is 10% to 15% of tuition, rounded to $1,000; arms are $0, half, and full.
Batch label and the seed record, documented before outcomes were known.
Same key as students. One row per recorded activity.
What the activity was.

description: Raw source label for the activity (Source 1, Source 2 and so on).
Date of the activity. Use to identify the first inquiry type.
Same hashed key as the other files.
ZIP5 of the permanent address at application. Blank if unknown. Used once by the append job, then deleted within 30 days of append QA.
Which address the ZIP comes from. A family address is common for applicants; tell us if you hold both.
Entering class year. Send the last three completed cycles.

State of the permanent address at application, as two-letter USPS codes. One row per state. Use XX for unknown and ZZ for outside the United States. Aggregate counts only. This is not the student-level `region_code`, and it carries no ZIP3.

LSAT band of the applicant, if you can aggregate by band. Leave blank for the all-bands row. Send your own band edges and tell us what they are. Include a row with a blank band if you send bands, so the rows sum to the state total.
allowed_values_or_notes: Your band label, as defined in your own reports

description: Applicants for the cohort, state and band, by the Applicant definition in this request. Send the count as it is, including small counts. Please do not suppress or round.
Applicants offered admission, including from the waiting list, by the Admitted definition in this request.
Admits who paid the first enrollment deposit and had not withdrawn by the cohort's census date. State which deposit you count if you use two.
Entering class year. Send the current cycle and the prior two.
Week number counted from the date applications opened for that cohort (week 1 is the first seven days). Same week number means the same point in the cycle.
Last day of that week.
Applications received from the application open date through the end of the week.
Offers of admission released through the end of the week.
First enrollment deposits received through the end of the week.
Entering class year. Include the last three completed years, the next entering class and each planned year after it.

Published annual JD tuition for that entering class, in dollars. Send the exact figure for the next entering class. If tuition differs by residency or program, send one row per entry year and tell us how it differs.
Change from the prior year, in percent, to the precision you have. Send the exact decided figure for the next entering class, not a rounded one.
Published annual undergraduate tuition at your university for the same year, in dollars. Used for the tuition comparison between your programs.
Target size of the entering JD class for that year.
Hard cap on the entering class for that year, if there is one. Leave blank if the target is soft.
Whether the tuition and class figures in the row are actual, decided but not yet published, or planned and still open to change.
